note: packing list of the robot's three struts as their modules reach the assembly cell: three strut cores, six motor modules, three bay lids, six end caps with covers (per strut: one core, two motor modules, one lid, two end caps)
frame_note: each model file is in its own frame, fixed by the module's own geometry (frame_rule); it is not the mounting frame and says nothing about where on the rod or at which turn about it the module is mounted
mass_note: nominal_mass_g is the module's nominal design value (the robot's model data, not a weighing); mass_is_estimate marks a value estimated by the stated rule
com_note: com_mm is the module's centre of mass in the frame of its model file, computed from its parts' materials and volumes and scaled to the nominal mass; the model files are visual tessellations (not watertight): do not integrate them
envelope_note: envelope_mm = the model file's extent along its x, y, z; box_mm = its two box corners
purchased_parts: purchased/purchased_parts.md (the bought parts inside the modules: vendors and part numbers)

M0.role: strut core: the electronics bay's base half with the main board and the boards on it, and the aluminium rod through it
M0.where: pre-assembled; the three cores are clamped in the cell's cradle (not handled by the robot)
M0.frame_rule: x = the rod axis; y, z follow the cross-section's minimum-area rectangle up to a small fixed turn about x; origin near the box centre (box_mm gives the box)
M0.material: black PLA bay half, green main board with small coloured boards and connectors on it, brass heat-set inserts, black screws, white nylon spacers, aluminium rod
M0.mass_basis: the bay's nominal mass less the lid's estimated share, plus the rod

M1.role: motor module: slides onto the rod, one on each side of the electronics bay
M1.where: loose, in the motor nests of the two parts trays
M1.frame_rule: x = the bore axis, + towards the end where the battery lead sticks out; y, z from the minimum-area rectangle of the cross-section; origin = box centre
M1.material: black PLA enclosures and winch, steel gearmotor, two LiPo pouch cells (the lead of one sticks out of the module's inner end), brass heat-set inserts, black screws, white nylon cable guide ring (M1a only)
M1.builds_note: the six motor modules are one design; three of them carry a small cable guide ring (model file parts/M1a_motor_module.stl), three do not (parts/M1b_motor_module.stl); the two model files share one frame, and any of the six fits either end of any rod

M2.role: bay lid: goes onto the electronics bay
M2.where: loose, in the lid nests of the left parts tray
M2.frame_rule: x = the long axis; y, z follow the cross-section's minimum-area rectangle up to a small fixed turn about x; origin near the box centre (box_mm gives the box)
M2.material: black PLA lid with its two long black screws
M2.mass_rule: estimate: share of the printed bay halves by solid volume

M3.role: end cap with its silicone cover: goes onto a rod end
M3.where: loose, in the cap nests of the two parts trays
M3.frame_rule: x = the bore axis, + towards the bore's opening; y, z from the minimum-area rectangle of the cross-section; origin = box centre
M3.material: grey resin cap, silicone cover (red, green or blue)
M3.covers_note: the six end caps are one design and differ only in the colour of their covers; on three of them the cover sits turned a little about the bore axis relative to the model file (the cover is a body of revolution: no visible difference)
